look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: in bloom, look for numerous small white-rayed, yellow-centered daisy heads (typically 50–100 narrow ray florets), ALTERNATE narrow upper stem leaves gradually getting shorter upward, and fine hairs lying mostly against/pointing up the stem (STRIGOSE). Look for persistent basal leaves. But don't identify on white flowers or 'untoothed leaves' alone: leaf margins can be entire OR toothed and E. annuus overlaps. Check leaf BASE: E. philadelphicus commonly clasps the stem, unlike the usually nonclasping stem leaves of E. strigosus. Horseweed E. canadensis has numerous MUCH smaller, almost rayless-looking fresh heads.

morphology_keys.habit: Erect/ascending annual, biennial or short-lived perennial; about 30–70 cm typically. Depending on variety, a simple fibrous-rooted crown or short rhizomes/basal tufts may occur. Do not force a single life cycle in Central Texas.
morphology_keys.leaves: Lower leaves often persist into flowering; basal spatulate to oblanceolate/linear, taper toward base. Alternate stem leaves generally narrow, gradually reduced toward branching top. Margins VARIABLE — entire, shallowly crenate or genuinely serrate. Leaf-only rule not decisive.
morphology_keys.leaf_base: Usually nonclasping upper leaves, in contrast to often auriculate/clasping E. philadelphicus. Take a true leaf-node side macro before using as firm species key.
morphology_keys.stems_hairs: Fine, typically upward-leaning/appressed strigose hairs (sometimes more spreading), versus often conspicuous spreading hairs on E. annuus. Hair direction needs a SHARP lateral close-up and is NOT verifiable from the installed photograph.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Numerous composite flower heads in a loose corymb-like to panicle-like branching array; bright yellow central disc florets and many narrow white (rarely pinkish/bluish) ray florets; ray lamina typically 4–6 mm; involucre ~2–4 mm HIGH by ~5–12 mm wide in FNA. Actual whole-head width varies; do not call involucre height head diameter.
morphology_keys.phyllaries: 2–4 overlapping ranks of narrow involucral bracts; pubescence varies. Need a sharp side image with a millimeter ruler; not shown sufficiently in existing site photo.
morphology_keys.fruit: Cypselae with different pappus pattern between ray and disc fruits (FNA); individual mature fruits and outer corona not photographed at usable scale here. Fruit macros especially useful with E. tenuis and strigosus complex.
morphology_keys.confusion: E. strigosus is variable and has recognized infraspecific taxa in FNA, including calcicolous types. None of the single source photos independently verifies a variety or Hays County population.

comparisons.look_here_first: Use THREE checkpoints together: how basal and upper stem leaves are shaped/attached, orientation of stem hairs (hand lens), and FRESH head size/ray length with scale. The existing exact-species photo is flower-focused and does NOT reveal the diagnostic roots, hairs, basal crown, or phyllaries.

field_key.separate: Many tiny greenish/pale heads in a strongly branched upper plume; very short barely visible fresh rays. Mature pappus looks white and fluffy but is not fresh flower rays.
field_key.photo: Installed existing horseweed photo 02 shows standing growth architecture; avoid using fruit photo 03 as fresh flower.

field_key.separate: Stem leaves often conspicuously clasp the stem at base, usually broader/coarser; heads often with more very fine rays (FNA 150–250+, compared with 50–100 in E. strigosus).
field_key.photo: Actual installed Philadelphia fleabane view included as compare-only; clasping base is not isolated in that image.

field_key.separate: Coarser/broader lower leaves that often wither before flowering, leafy mid-stem and commonly more outwardly spreading stem hairs; overlaps exist.
field_key.photo: Need verified same-scale annuus and strigosus stem-hair + basal-leaf paired photographs.

field_key.separate: Annual slender taproot with showy fewer large heads, lower stem hairs spreading/deflexed; don't force from white rays alone.
field_key.photo: Existing geiseri card/gallery can be studied separately.

cautions: Very narrow leaves and appressed hair are helpful, not immutable binary traits across all populations.
A small white daisy head is shared across many Asteraceae; not a diagnosis by itself.
The installed Chris Stahl image is sourced as E. strigosus but alone cannot independently resolve variety, leaf-base details, stem hair angles or root system.
The look-alike panels are correctly labeled OTHER species, not additional E. strigosus source photographs.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.title: Prairie fleabane — the thin-petaled daisy with a fine-hair clue

stages.title: ONE: inspect the whole plant
stages.description: Do not start and stop at white daisies. Look for lower leaves that persist while flowering and more narrow, gradually smaller alternate stem leaves above.

stages.title: TWO: inspect one intact leaf attachment
stages.description: Photograph stem NODE at right angle. A clearly clasping upper leaf suggests E. philadelphicus instead. One flower photo is not enough to establish this trait.

stages.title: THREE: inspect stem hairs with a hand lens
stages.description: Look on the lower-to-middle stem in side view; hairs usually lean close to/up the stem in strigosus, while E. annuus often has spreading hairs. A blurred stem should be marked unscorable.

stages.title: FOUR: inspect a fresh head and its green cup
stages.description: Numerous narrow white (occasionally pale pinkish) rays around a yellow disc; measure actual fresh rays and cup height. Compare with horseweed's much tinier heads and Philadelphia fleabane's often numerous extra rays.

stages.title: FIVE: reserve difficult fruit questions for a macro
stages.description: Fruit outer pappus traits may be important in E. strigosus versus close taxa, but do not infer pappus ring counts from a flower picture.

glossary.capitulum: One composite daisy 'flower head', built from many small florets.
glossary.rays: Strap-shaped outer florets, resembling thin petals; commonly white in this species.
glossary.disc: Cluster of tubular central florets making the yellow center.
glossary.phyllary: A green bract in the small cup (involucre) immediately underneath a daisy head.
glossary.strigose: Having short, straight-ish hairs typically lying flat or nearly flat along a surface.
glossary.clasping: A leaf base that partly wraps around the stem at its point of attachment.
glossary.corymbiform: Flower cluster in which many head-bearing branches create a loosely level or rounded top.
glossary.cypsela: Dry one-seeded fruit of the aster family.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.memory_rule: Thin white rays + yellow centers? That's just the START. Check ALTERNATE leaves → how upper leaf joins stem → fine hair direction → the fresh head. Horseweed is a TINY-head plume; Philadelphia usually has CLASPING upper leaves.

part_examples.title: 1 · PRAIRIE FLEABANE — white ray, yellow disc
part_examples.look_for: The radiating white narrow straplike florets surround a yellow central disc; this is one composite head.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Recognize the aster family flower anatomy before narrowing to species.

part_examples.title: 2 · PRAIRIE FLEABANE — closed head (not fruit)
part_examples.look_for: The small erect pale buds on same shoot are unopened heads; don't claim cypselae/fruit before maturity.
part_examples.why_it_matters: A bud is not a seedhead, which is especially useful after the horseweed fruit-stage correction.

part_examples.title: 3 · NEED PHOTO — nonclasping node and stem hairs
part_examples.role: leaf base and appressed stem hair macro
part_examples.look_for: Take one unbroken leaf attachment and a sharp side view of mid-stem hairs with a mm ruler, ideally beside confirmed E. annuus or E. philadelphicus.
part_examples.why_it_matters: This is the decisive missing separator, and cannot be verified in current photo.

part_examples.title: 4 · NEED PHOTO — full plant with basal leaves
part_examples.look_for: Full specimen including stem, top branches and intact lower leaves (show variable entire/toothed margins), plus scale.
part_examples.why_it_matters: A flower-only picture can mislead about species, leaf size and seasonal stage.

part_examples.title: 5 · NEED PHOTO — phyllaries and pappus
part_examples.role: fresh involucre side + ripe fruit microscope
part_examples.look_for: Separately photograph a fresh head side, green phyllary cup and actual ripe cypsela with outer corona at millimeter scale.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Needed to resolve more difficult E. strigosus / E. tenuis complex and varieties.
